note: The closed run record for the a2aproject/A2A#1631 discovery interop with ziolndr's ARBITER. It records the order ARBITER returned over the trust-filter permitted set, completing evidence -> permitted -> order -> recorded result. NENRIN records the order unchanged; it did not produce the order or the permitted set and computes no score. ARBITER produced the order; the reference trust filter produced permitted; NENRIN supplied the evidence. The frozen input fixture is left unmodified so the commit the ordering party verified stays the anchor.

frozen_input.nenrin_offline_verification: PASS, verified by the ordering party against the frozen fixture

permitted_by: reference-trust-filter-v0 (example policy, not NENRIN): a witness disagreement is carried into permitted so the orderer weighs it; a provider equivocation is fail-closed and excluded

order_by.note: cand_bravo reached the orderer with its witness disagreement still present (disagreement_hops = 1); cand_charlie was excluded upstream by the reference trust filter for provider equivocation and never entered the ordering field. Scores are ARBITER output, recorded here verbatim, not computed by NENRIN.

counterfactual_reported_by_arbiter.description: one-variable ablation by the ordering party on the same frozen fixture and compare path: cand_bravo nenrin_evidence.disagreement_hops changed 1 -> 0, all else held constant
counterfactual_reported_by_arbiter.claim: the orderer is sensitive to the surfaced disagreement_hops field under a one-variable change; this does not establish witness disagreement as a general cause of ranking, and does not move the trust or authorization decision into the orderer

boundary: evidence (NENRIN) -> permitted (reference trust filter, not NENRIN) -> order (ARBITER) -> recorded result (this record). NENRIN computed no permitted, no order and no score. It records the order ARBITER returned, unchanged, and can anchor this record so a third party recomputes each step rather than trusting the operator.

open_ordering.role: the NENRIN composition is the executable reference example for keeping evidence, permission, and task-specific ordering as separate interoperable boundaries

does_not_establish: that the returned order is correct or optimal: NENRIN records it, it does not judge it
any trust score from NENRIN: none is computed here, and the scores shown are ARBITER output recorded verbatim
that NENRIN produced the order or the permitted set: ARBITER produced the order, the reference trust filter produced permitted, NENRIN supplied the evidence
